title: Malted rye rolls
subtitle: soft, dark-crumbed rolls made with rye flour and malt extract
excerpt: Malted rye rolls are soft, dark-crumbed bread rolls made with a blend of rye flour and strong white flour, enriched with malt extract. The malt extract deepens the flavour and gives the crust a dark mahogany colour. The rye flour makes the dough sticky and the crumb dense and moist; the rolls keep better than white bread rolls and are still good the day after baking.
sourceNotes: Rye and malt breads are documented in German, Scandinavian, and British baking traditions from the medieval period onward. Malted brown rolls with rye are a staple of British artisan bakeries from the late twentieth century.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze baked rolls in a sealed bag for up to 2 months. Reheat from frozen in a hot oven for 8 minutes.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Shape the rolls and refrigerate overnight for a slow second proof. Remove 1 hour before baking.
recipe.temperatureNote: fan 200 degrees C / gas 7, with steam for the first 10 minutes

baking.steamMethod: tray of boiling water in the base of the oven

content.text: Malted rye rolls use a mix of rye flour and strong white flour with malt extract. Rye flour absorbs more water than white flour and makes the dough stickier and denser; do not add extra flour to compensate. The malt extract goes directly into the dough and gives the rolls a deep, slightly sweet caramel flavour and a dark colour. Steam at the start of baking helps the crust colour and develop.

Mix both flours with the instant yeast and salt. Add the malt extract, olive oil, and warm water. Mix until a sticky dough forms. Knead for 8 minutes; the dough will remain sticker than white bread dough throughout. Do not add extra flour.
Cover and leave to rise in a warm place for 90 minutes until doubled. Rye dough rises more slowly than white dough.

Using wet hands, divide the dough into 10 equal pieces and shape each into a round. The wet hands prevent the dough sticking without adding flour. Place on a lined baking tray, spacing them 4 cm apart. Mist the tops lightly with water and scatter with rolled oats if using.
Cover loosely and leave to prove for 45 to 50 minutes until visibly puffed.
Heat the oven to 220 degrees C (fan 200 degrees C / gas 7). Place a deep roasting tin in the base of the oven and pour in a kettle of boiling water just before loading the rolls.
Bake for 20 to 22 minutes until the rolls have a dark, mahogany crust and sound hollow when tapped underneath. Cool on a rack.

attrs.problem: Dough refuses to hold a shape and spreads on the tray
attrs.avoid: Avoid trying to shape rye dough the same way as white dough; it is much sticker and has less gluten structure.
attrs.fix: Use wet hands to portion and shape. Accept that the rolls will be slightly flat compared to white rolls; the rye flour gives less lift. Space them further apart so they rise slightly more freely.

attrs.problem: Crust very dark but interior still gummy
attrs.avoid: Avoid judging doneness by crust colour alone; rye bread goes dark quickly but the interior takes longer to bake through.
attrs.fix: Test with a digital thermometer: the interior should reach 93 to 96 degrees C. Tent loosely with foil and bake a further 5 minutes if the outside is dark but the inside is not done.
